creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Follow on from `make-interaction` (a_25Rcu1uOI). Reproduced against v0.11.0.

A filtered `pick` that narrows to a single option selects it without prompting, and discards whatever `--reply` was supplied:

```rad
target = pick(services, svc_filter, prefer_exact=true)   // line 11
```

```
rad 06_filter.rad api --reply 11:worker
  -> tailing api    EXIT=0
```

`worker` was an explicit instruction. It was dropped for `api` with no error.

RAD20046 does warn up front - `pick options computed at runtime  filtered - may not prompt, and then ignores its answer` - so the behavior is disclosed. What stays silent is the moment the two actually disagree, which is the only moment it matters. It is also data-dependent: the same command is right or wrong depending on what the filtered list holds that day.

### Direction

Fail when an auto-selected value isn't an exact match for the supplied `--reply`; stay quiet when they agree.

That leans on a distinction worth confirming first. `--reply-na` already means "I assert this won't prompt", and fails loudly when it does. If a real `--reply` symmetrically means "I expect to be asked", the two become complementary: `--reply-na` says "I expect this to narrow to one", `--reply` says "I expect a choice". The RAD20046 hint already steers toward `--reply-na` for filtered picks, so this mostly makes existing advice enforceable.
title: A filtered pick discards a disagreeing --reply and picks something else
